issues: whether an employee terminated without cause is entitled to damages representing bonus/LTIP payments that would have vested during the reasonable notice period

whether an 'actively employed' eligibility clause in an incentive plan is sufficiently clear and unambiguous to rebut the presumptive entitlement to damages for lost incentive compensation during the notice period
whether such a clause was brought to the employee's attention so as to be enforceable
how reasonable notice period is calculated for the purposes of assessing damages that would include the incentive plan payout
whether the incentive plan is a 'wage' or otherwise governed by employment standards legislation restricting termination-related exclusions
key_facts: client participated in a long-term incentive plan (LTIP)
the LTIP would have paid out during what should have been the reasonable notice period
the plan contains an 'actively employed' eligibility requirement to qualify for payout
causes_of_action: breach of contract (failure to pay damages in lieu of reasonable notice, including lost incentive compensation)
search_terms: actively employed clause bonus notice period
damages in lieu of notice bonus entitlement
needs_clarification: What province or jurisdiction governs the employment relationship (e.g., where the employee worked/was employed), and is the employer federally regulated?
